title: Row 1, the identifier. Settled: a monotonic integer, allocated only by the data owner and declared AUTOINCREMENT so a value is never reused and never renumbered
Opaque by rule: no surface, agent, or plugin may interpret an id, compare ids, or assume adjacency; that rule is what satisfies RULE-ID-1's word "opaque"
Display convention, presentation only: TSK-0001 for tasks and PRJ-0001 for projects, the prefix marking the record kind so a wrong-kind reference fails loudly; padding is a minimum width...
The parser accepts the prefix or the bare number, case-insensitively
The export and the change log carry the bare integers; a restore by file copy keeps sqlite_sequence with them
A future import must set the sequence to the highest id it carries before accepting a write
A test that deletes a record and asserts the next id does not reuse it belongs in the first ticket that touches the store
Row 2, the title. Settled: keep §3.2 as written. Required, 1 to 500 characters; it now carries the identity of the task
Row 3, the description. Settled: replaced by notes, the append-only journal idea applied to text
The name is note, not Taskwarrior's annotation, because it is the word a person uses and the one the MCP tool will carry
A note is multi-line with a length cap, and carries its own creation timestamp
Note display order is timestamp then id
A note may be removed, and the removal is a change in the operation log, so the text survives in history
A correction is a new note
Recorded deviation from the frozen specification: §3.2's optional description is gone, and the map and the architecture document carry the deviation
The export carries a list where it carried a string
Row 14, date gating. Settled: refused in v1, and named as a first change after v1
It is recorded as the smaller of the two post-v1 changes, so it is the first unless an order is decided otherwise
The shape it would take is one date, "not before", not Taskwarrior's trio of wait, scheduled, and until
Date gating needs its own grilling rather than a field added quietly
Row 15, recurrence. Settled: refused in v1, and named as a change after v1; nothing changes about v1 scope
The reference shape is Taskwarrior's: a template record plus instances, with a per-instance status ledger on the template
Recurrence is the second named change after v1, which keeps a later debate anchored to a decided order
Date gating and recurrence are refused for v1 but queued right after it; tags, user-defined attributes, urgency, and annotations are refused without a scheduled return
Tags, row 4: none in v1. Revisit trigger: the user wants a cross-project cut such as "everything waiting on someone else"
Projects stay as §3.3 writes them
User-defined attributes, row 13: none, and no extension point in the record; the post-v1 plugin story gives an extension with a port, a configuration schema, and validation
Urgency, row 5: none. The 1 to 5 priority stays the only importance signal, after deadline and dependency pressure
Statuses, row 11: the five stored statuses plus derived blocked stay
The inbox against ready split stays, and it is where the estimate becomes required
History leaves the task record and lives in the operation log
Requirements are a product rule rather than a storage constraint, with one deliberate exception: the store enforces identity, status, and the timestamps
The reconciled record: an identifier, a required title, zero or more notes, an optional project reference, a priority, an estimate, an optional deadline, source metadata, a stored status...
Priority is 1 to 5, defaulting to 3
The estimate is in positive whole minutes, required before a task is ready or in progress
The deadline is optional and its effective value is the earlier of task and project
Source metadata is a type defaulting to manual, an optional reference, and an optional URL
Stored status is inbox, ready, in progress, completed, or cancelled, with blocked derived and never stored
The one deviation from the frozen specification: §3.2's optional description is replaced by notes
The identifier's concreteness is not a deviation: §3.14 allows any stable opaque identifier
Sealed in the record so the child efforts do not have to rediscover it
